identity: Dutch full-time 2026–2027 VU standard route, taught with UvA through ACASA. The approved OER Articles 11.3 and 11.4 govern required credits.
progression: The Dutch full-time 2026–2027 VU bachelor (RIO56003) is taught in the ACASA VU–UvA collaboration on the UvA campus. There are no formal specialisations. The adopted OER Articles11.1–11.4 establish ten compulsory6EC first-year units, thirteen compulsory6EC later units, a12EC thesis including colloquium and30EC genuine open study:180EC. The standard programme is used, not the shortened UvA-entry pathway or pre2017 transition. Comedy is an optional additional6EC module, as the visible Appendix4 footnote confirms, despite appearing unqualified on recruitment pages; it is not added to the compulsory total. Article9.1 requires a positive BSA for post-first-year assessment, subject to catalogue conditions; thesis entry requires all first- and second-year courses. Article14.1 normally requires48first-yearEC for a positive full-time BSA. Article10.4 requires a Dutch diagnostic test and, on failure, the remedial course, outside180EC. Article11.5 requires85% attendance for Historical Sources, Philosophy of the Humanities, ACASA Excursion and Reception/Creative Writing, otherwise repeat or an additional assignment. Article12.1 allows a minor, electives, study abroad or up to12EC internship; outside VU/UvA needs examination-board approval. Normally at most12EC introductory study, exceptionally24EC for specified VU/UvA minors or one-language acquisition packages; foreign language-improvement courses outside an academic degree do not qualify. Minor course prerequisites still apply. Optional honours are additional, not part of180EC. Thesis is disciplinary research; Article3.10 guarantees draft feedback under the thesis regulation. Programme tutoring occurs at least twice per year (Article7.3).
internalReconciliation: Appendix 4 gives code L_AABAGLT308 for the required Historiography title where the adopted table gives L_AABAGLT305. It gives L_AABAAGO201 for Philosophy of the Humanities where the adopted table gives L_AABAAGO203. Matching titles and credits and joint programme descriptions support each as one requirement. Neither code is used in the reader-facing table. Appendix 4 expressly marks Comedy additional.
